questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curve ahead.
Roadwork ahead.
Merging traffic.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the road will curve ahead.

questions.question: It is important to be alert to motorcycles because:

options.text: They are more difficult to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more difficult to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is or how fast it is moving. Always watch carefully around motorcyclists.

questions.question: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must proceed straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer have to turn in the direction that the arrow indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow's direction. But first, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass.

questions.question: Newer vehicles are equipped with a brake warning lamp on the instrument panel. This lamp:

options.text: Should come on when the parking brake is released.
Comes on to indicate that the brake system is defective.
Will never come on.
Comes on to indicate that the brake lights are operational.

questions.correctAnswerText: Comes on to indicate that the brake system is defective.
questions.explanation: The brake warning lamp should turn off when you release the parking brake. If it stays on when you press the brake pedal, your brake system has a problem. Do not drive the vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
An upcoming curve in the road.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: The most common color of warning signs is:

options.text: Red.
Yellow.
Green.
Blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped, yellow, and have black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected conditions on the road ahead.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you are fully in the exit lane.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when you:

options.text: Have to stop quickly.
Are passing another car.
Have lost control of your car.
Are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to stay away from you.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes display arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A solid yellow arrow:

options.text: Is never used as a traffic signal.
Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.
Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.
Tells drivers that a green arrow is about to be shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and be ready to stop when you see it.

questions.question: You are making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street. When you have completed the turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the right lane of the street.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane of the street.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane of the street.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, complete your turn into the lane closest to the one you just left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, no matter what.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross safely. Pay attention to people crossing at intersections or turning into them.

questions.question: Alcohol affects you:

options.text: Faster after you have just eaten.
Faster on an empty stomach.
The same way every time.
Only if you drink more than two drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster on an empty stomach.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects you differently depending on whether you have eaten. Drinking on an empty stomach affects you faster. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Slow down and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is coming, move to the right side of the road as far as possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheel away from the curb when parking uphill. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal right before you turn or change lanes.
Signal 100 feet ahead before turning or changing lanes, even if no cars are around.
Signal 100 feet ahead, but only when there is traffic.
Any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal 100 feet ahead before turning or changing lanes, even if no cars are around.
questions.explanation: Always signal every time you turn or change lanes. Signal 100 feet ahead, even if there are no other cars.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is danger.
Tell you what you must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn you that a school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing rules, and other driving rules.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow on a traffic light, you:

options.text: Should merge into the lane the arrow shows.
Should slow down and stop if it is safe.
May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
May drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane. Let any cars and pedestrians already in the intersection go first.

questions.question: Leave extra space when stopping:

options.text: On a hill.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll booth.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward, extra space helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: At a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Slow down and carefully drive through.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. Then drive forward when traffic is clear.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb:

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This keeps your car from rolling into traffic if it starts to roll.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you must stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep your current speed until you enter the reduced speed zone.
Start to slow down your vehicle.
Do not slow down because traffic will back up.
You may slow down if you want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start to slow down your vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to start slowing down. The new speed limit will begin at the next speed limit sign.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the car radio before backing up to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: It is hard to see behind a vehicle. Before you get in the driver's seat, walk to the back of the vehicle and check for children and small objects.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to do when driving on a curve?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the posted speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle may be hard to control on a curve due to inertia. You must slow down before entering the curve to stay in control.

questions.question: What are bicyclists required to do?

options.text: Obey traffic signs, signals, and laws.
Ride on the sidewalk in business districts.
Ride in the center of traffic lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs, signals, and laws.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are legal vehicles. Bicyclists must obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws just like car drivers.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show drivers directions and distances.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show directions and distances to help you find your way when driving.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm upward, they are signaling that they intend to turn right. Change your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: You and another vehicle arrive at an intersection with no traffic signs or signals at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
The biggest vehicle
The vehicle that enters the intersection first

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the right
questions.explanation: The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Once that vehicle has safely passed through, the other vehicle may go.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only if they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not be able to stop in time.
